name: Walkies
subtitle: Uncover your suburb on foot
promotionalText: Your suburb starts under clouds and every street you walk clears a bit more. Getting to 100% is a lot harder than it sounds, which is half the fun.
description:
Walkies hides your suburb under clouds on a satellite map. Go for a walk and the clouds clear off every street you walk down. The idea is to get your whole suburb to 100%, which is a lot harder than it sounds, and a good excuse to go down streets you've never bothered with.

HOW IT WORKS
Add your suburb or town and it turns up under a blanket of cloud, split into hex tiles about 90 metres across. Your streets and paths are dotted over the top so you can plan where to go. Walk through a tile and it clears. Only tiles with a street or path through them count, so you're never stuck needing to swim across a lake.

WALKING ONLY
Bikes, cars and buses don't count, and neither does anything faster than a jog. Walkies uses the phone's motion chip to tell the difference, so no clearing tiles from the car window (I did think about it).

ALWAYS ON, IF YOU LIKE
Let Walkies use your location "Always" and it notices when you head out on foot and records the walk by itself, then stops after ten minutes of not moving. GPS pauses while you're sitting still. Or leave it off and just press Start walk when you go.

SECRETS UNDER THE CLOUDS
Little stories about local history, Wardandi Noongar heritage and nature are hidden under the tiles, with nothing on the map to give them away. Walk over one and it goes in your sticker book. Right now there are over a hundred of them around Busselton in Western Australia, and I'm hoping to add more places over time.

AFTER EVERY WALK
A little replay shows the tiles you uncovered, how far your suburb has come and a guess at how many more walks it'll take to finish. Each walk keeps its distance and step count.

SHELLS, LEVELS AND QUESTS
New tiles earn shells and XP. Spend shells on hats for your marker, different clouds and a spyglass for peeking at where a secret might be, and pick up a few quests each week.

TEAMS
Start a team with your mates and send them an invite link. Your clouds and secrets stay yours.

WORKS OFFLINE
Everything's saved on your phone first, and backs up to your account when there's signal, so a new phone gets it all back. Sign in with Apple or Google. No ads and no tracking.

The idea came from my mate James. It's just me making it, so if something's broken or you've got an idea, tap "Suggest a feature" in Settings, or email walkies@mikecann.app.

ageRating._note: Walkies has no objectionable content: a map, your walks, and short local-history stories. Nobody can see anything anyone else writes except team names and members' names inside an invite-only team. Unknown keys are skipped, and keys Apple adds later are left as they are.

review.notes:
Thanks for taking a look at Walkies.

SIGNING IN
Sign-up is open to anyone, so no demo account is needed. Tap "Sign in with Apple" or "Sign in with Google" on the first screen and you get a new, empty account of your own.

THE FIRST RUN
After signing in, a short setup asks for location (with Motion & Fitness), then notifications, and says what each is for before iOS asks. It switches on "Always on" (Settings > Always on), where Walkies notices you've started walking and records the walk by itself, using the motion chip and region monitoring. That's what location "Always" is for, and it's optional:
- With "While Using the App", or with Always on switched off in Settings, everything works the same, and you press Start walk on the map to record a walk. The location background mode keeps a walk you started recording with the phone locked in a pocket.
- Motion & Fitness tells walking from cycling or driving, and counts steps.
- Notifications are local only: a secret found while the phone is in your pocket.

TRYING IT WITHOUT WALKING A SUBURB
1. On the map, tap the place chip at the top left, then "Add a place", and search for any suburb or town, for example "Cupertino" or "Fremantle". Its outline and streets come from OpenStreetMap, and it appears under clouds split into hex tiles. Streets are dotted over the clouds. The first fetch of a place can take up to a minute.
2. Turn off Settings > Always on, so the map shows a Start walk button. Tap it and walk a little way down a street (a minute or two is plenty). Tiles you pass through turn orange and the clouds lift off them. Faster than about 12 km/h, or in a vehicle, doesn't count. (With Always on, just start walking instead.)
3. Tap End walk to see the replay of the walk and the tiles it uncovered. It's then in the Walks tab, and the Progress tab shows the shells and XP it earned.
In the Simulator you can do the same with Features > Location > City Walk.

The Secrets tab lists stories that are hidden under tiles. They only exist around Busselton, Western Australia for now, so elsewhere the book shows them as not found yet. The rest of the app works anywhere.

DELETING THE ACCOUNT
Settings > Delete account. It asks twice, deletes everything from the server, clears the phone and signs out.

OTHER
- "Suggest a feature" in Settings opens a feedback form. The microphone and speech recognition are only used if you record a voice note there. Requests are only visible to the person who sent them and to me.
- Teams (from the place chip on the map) are invite-only, with a name, colour and photo for each member.
- No ads, no tracking, no in-app purchases. Shells are earned by walking and can't be bought.
